author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A small plane overshot the runway at Richmond Airport late Wednesday morning and came to rest nose-down along Heaton Orchard Road, according to local officials.

Emergency crews were called at about 11:40 a.m. The Piper Cub damaged a fence during the incident, but the two occupants got out on their own and were not injured. NBC 10 reported that the pair were a couple from New Jersey.

Officials said the pilot had not previously landed at Richmond and had diverted there from Quonset. The aircraft remained visibly damaged near the roadway as police and firefighters secured the area and began documenting what happened.

Heaton Orchard Road was closed near the airport while crews worked at the scene. The Rhode Island Airport Corporation was expected to provide additional information. The absence of injuries limited the immediate human toll, but investigators will still need to determine why the landing continued beyond the runway.
dek: A Piper Cub came to rest nose-down on Heaton Orchard Road after an attempted landing late Wednesday morning.
headline: Small plane overshoots Richmond runway; two occupants uninjured
